correctness.rationale: For a g-invariant independent face S, its contribution to the reduced alternating oriented simplex trace equals minus (-1) to the number of g-cycles in S. Fixing original selected vertices, the new-vertex signed enumerator factors by edge cycles. A non-inverted edge cycle yields the independence evaluation at -1 of a path on three, two, or one remaining orbit vertices: respectively -1, -1, or 0. An inverted edge cycle has two internal vertex orbits (one outer, one middle) and yields -1 when endpoints are absent, or 0 when both are selected. Thus each edge cycle contributes -1 precisely for original independent selections. Multiplication gives the sign (-1) to the number of edge cycles and hence the claimed reduced Lefschetz identity. Csorba (2009), Section 3 and Theorem 11, supplies the non-equivariant degree shift; equality of finite-group rational characters yields the claimed single-degree representation. The independent verifier directly constructs lifted graph automorphisms and signed orbit-conflict enumeration for 251 actions, 70 of them direct edge inversions.

originality.rationale: The inspected seven-page Csorba (2009) paper gives ordinary homotopy suspensions, not the signed edge-action trace and rational representation. The characteristic correction for edge inversions requires a separate signed invariant-face computation; the source does not assert an equivariant map or character formula. Related published statements on specialized subdivided multitheta graphs, Kneser graph representations, and other graph symmetry modules concern distinct objects or narrower actions. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a guarantee against unindexed or implicit equivalences.

value.rationale: A complete operation-level character identity has mathematical purpose beyond a formal consequence of nonequivariant suspension: homotopy type alone loses action signs. The edge cycle parity handles arbitrary graph automorphisms, including endpoint reversals, uniformly. Under a natural single-degree hypothesis it yields the full rational homology representation from the original one; for the complete graph K_n the answer is the edge sign (sign of labels to power n-2) times the standard augmentation representation in a degree growing quadratically in n. This is a genuine infinite-family symmetry refinement, not a finite sample or textbook sphere count.
